question.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}{y}^{3}\,i+{y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,j,\,∇\cdot G=-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x).
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G) & =∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)+∇\cdot (4G) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+2G) & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+4\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =x{y}^{3}+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =x{y}^{3}-y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
